why: AC2 and AC3 of RWB-E3-010 end with the case in BOOKED_IN_ALS_NLEADS and PLAN_RUNNING, while Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the case and its state to rwb-case and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables.

text: The booking confirmation is EV-11 rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1 consumed through this service's own inbox and decided by the BOOKING_MATCH package in force; the booking date and the schedule basis are read from v_ace_plan and v_ace_payment and written on the seven schedule columns of treatment. The plan timers of R-RES-25 are durable timers inside TreatmentWorkflow, one per due date from the first due date at the cadence in force, with no timer row and no Schedule; they are named planInstallmentClock and planEndTimer.
why: TSD S2 T3.1 has no schedule or booking entity, the legacy build took an in-process callback unstructured by any source, Architecture v5 slide 42 names rwb-treatment a consumer of EV-11 and retires TimerDue in favour of timers inside the workflow, and the timer table is rwb-case's under DP-01.

text: The booking body carries nleadsRef, alsBookingRef, bookedAt, firstDueDate, installmentCount, installmentAmount, installmentsPaid and bookingDifference. The first seven are required because R-RES-22 needs both acknowledgements and R-RES-25 needs a first due date; bookingDifference is optional. Only nleadsRef has a column for its reference, so the ALS reference is carried on the booking record and the decision record and no column is created for it.
why: No source publishes a booking element, TSD S2 T3.1 marks the schedule columns as not required at column level, R-RES-22 confirms on both acknowledgements, and the table carries nleads_ref only.
